title: Unicode confusable skeleton, normalization-version, and cross-artifact identifier tribunal
hypothesis: A pinned, curated identifier tribunal can detect deliberately confusable or normalization-colliding synthetic identifiers across phase artifacts and can reject ambiguous cross-file references without banning natural-language content or claiming complete spoof resistance.
falsifier: Mutate script mix, skeleton, normalization form, case fold, default-ignorable placement, joining-control context, Unicode version, protected-ID collision, natural-language scope, and completeness claims; reject ambiguous identifiers while preserving ordinary prose.
